analysis.title: Market Insights Weekly, 20 November 2026
key_insights: Elevated inflation tied to the Middle East conflict has not eased. Central bank rhetoric stays hawkish on concern about second-round effects, meaning inflation broadening beyond energy.
The recent fall in global oil prices has not produced a significant decline in government bond yields (Chart 1).
The global equity sell-off continued, led by the AI technology sector. Anthropic's IPO briefly valued the company at $2 trillion and did not stop the decline.

Minutes of the Fed's October meeting indicated officials expect further tightening will be required. Markets fully discount a 25bp hike next month and further rises in 2027. Some rate-setters raised the possibility of a larger-than-usual increase.

Eurozone headline CPI accelerated to 4.0% in October, confirming the flash estimate. Core was revised up to 2.6% from 2.5%. Markets put the probability of a third ECB rate rise in December at more than 90%.

UK October CPI rose to 3.6% from 3.5%. Services CPI held at 3.7%, below the forecast of 3.8%, and labour data showed little sign of accelerating wage growth. The market-implied probability of a December BoE hike fell to about 75% from 80% at the start of the week.
Cornwall Insight estimates the Ofgem price cap, announced 25 November, will rise 26% in January to £2,166 for a typical household. This is expected to lift UK inflation at the start of next year.

BoE Governor Bailey said the BoE remains focused on energy prices spreading to other prices. MPC members appear before the Treasury Committee on Wednesday. Markets will look for guidance on whether pricing for back-to-back hikes is appropriate.
Lloyds forecasts the November UK composite PMI at 53.0 (previous 52.9) and the Eurozone composite at 52.1 (previous 51.7). France may stay in contraction.
US October CPI was stronger than expected: headline +0.4% m/m and core +0.3% m/m. Core has risen 0.3% for a third consecutive month, consistent with annualised inflation near 4%.
Lloyds forecasts October PCE at +0.3% m/m headline and core, taking y/y rates to 3.8% and 3.2% from 3.6% and 3.1%. Core PCE y/y has been above 2% since February 2021.
The second estimate of US Q3 GDP is expected to confirm strong growth, supported by AI investment, and could be revised up to 3.5% annualised.
US markets are closed Thursday 26 November for Thanksgiving and close early Friday.

tension_points.bull_case: Hawkish case: Governor Bailey stresses focus on energy prices spreading to other prices, and the market still prices about a 75% chance of a December hike.
tension_points.bear_case: Services CPI came in at 3.7% against a 3.8% forecast and labour data showed little wage acceleration, so the MPC may be able to wait until early next year.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Remarks from Bailey and Lombardelli at the Treasury Committee on Wednesday that show scope to wait would weaken the case for back-to-back hikes.
